extracted.intended_audience: students, reformers, policymakers, and readers interested in representative government and electoral reform
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and practical requirements for constructing a representative democracy that guards against class domination, improves the intellectual quality of representatives, and ensures fair proportional representation of minorities. Includes a detailed endorsement and explanation of Thomas Hare's quota/transfer electoral scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design governments for human beings as they are
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments must be made for human beings as they are, or as they are capable of speedily becoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base a constitution on the expectation that average citizens or office-holders will act from exalted disinterested motives; instead, account for ordinary self-interest, short-sightedness, and common fallacies when designing institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against corruption by power
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of power tends to foster selfish and immediate interests, corrupting men and classes and weakening habits of foresight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should include checks and securities to prevent those who hold power from using it for their own class advantage or indulging malign passions; anticipate that power will change behaviour and accommodate safeguards accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent class legislation / dominant-class preponderance
rubrics_metrics.description: No class, and no combination of classes likely to combine, shall be able to exercise a preponderant influence in the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The representative system must be organized so that sectional interests cannot carry measures against the combined opposition of other sectional interests and those guided by broader motives; avoid arrangements that allow a single class majority to enact lasting harm to other classes or posterity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance representation between major socioeconomic sections
rubrics_metrics.description: In a modern community the two main sections (roughly: manual laborers and employers/affinities) should be so arranged in the representative system that they influence about an equal number of votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a structural balance so that the selfish majority of any one class cannot prevail unchecked; preserve a minority of those guided by reason, justice, and general interest who can ally with parts of the majority to check sectional excesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation must be proportional to numbers (adequate minority representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a really equal democracy every section would be represented proportionately — a majority of electors would have a majority of representatives and a minority a corresponding minority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal suffrage implies that every individual should count equally; avoid electoral machinery that effectively blots out minorities or converts a numerical majority into a ruling privileged class of a subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not cure democratic evils by restricting the franchise; reform representation instead
rubrics_metrics.description: The common mode of attempting to avoid democratic evils is by limiting the democratic character through restricted suffrage, but this is a flawed response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than disenfranchising people, modify the electoral system (e.g., by proportional methods) to mitigate low intelligence in representation and class-legislation risks without sacrificing democratic principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a quota-based transferable-vote scheme (Hare's plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit of representation (quota) is the average number of voters per seat; any candidate who obtains that quota is returned, and votes may be counted from across constituencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanics recommended: compute quota by dividing total voters by seats; permit electors to vote for any candidate nationwide; allow ranked preferences; count first, second, third preferences centrally; allocate only up to the quota to any elected candidate and transfer surplus; use lot-drawing for tie-breaking if needed; keep full counting records publicly accessible so returns can be verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow voters to rank multiple preferences and transfer votes
rubrics_metrics.description: An elector may deliver a voting paper containing other names in addition to his first preference; if the first choice fails or has surplus, the vote counts for the next preferred candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable lists of preferences so defeated or surplus votes are not wasted; this helps minorities and dispersed supporters combine to return representatives, improving the efficacy of votes and representation of minority opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap votes counted per candidate to the quota and redistribute surplus
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than the quota of votes should be counted for any one candidate; the remainder (surplus) of votes counted for popular candidates is allocated to other candidates according to preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents a few extremely popular candidates from monopolizing representation and allows votes that would otherwise be wasted to help elect additional representatives; various practical methods exist for determining which specific votes are used for return and which are freed for transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit cross-district candidacy and pooled nationwide votes
rubrics_metrics.description: Votes would be given locally, but any elector would be at liberty to vote for any candidate, in whatever part of the country he might offer himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing electors to support candidates outside their locality lets minorities unable to win local contests help return national figures they prefer, and enables national reputation to assist independent and able candidates lacking local influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve local representation where valuable, but prioritize persons over places
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is worth preserving in the representation of places would be preserved; but members should represent persons, not merely the bricks and mortar of a town.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where local constituencies contain more voters than a quota, local representation will remain; minorities should be able to seek representation elsewhere. The goal is a stronger, more meaningful tie between electors and their representatives based on choice, not on local patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase intellectual quality of representatives via electoral design
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that allows dispersed minorities to combine votes for nationally known able men will bring into Parliament many independent, distinguished persons otherwise excluded by local influence and party machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the electoral rules (ranking, cross-district voting, quotas) to encourage able, independent candidates to stand by giving them a fair chance to attract scattered support; this increases the presence and influence of leading minds in the legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure transparency and auditability of the count
rubrics_metrics.description: The voting papers, and all the elements of the calculation, would be placed in public repositories, accessible to all whom they concerned; it would be easy to prove if any one was not duly returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized counting with full public records makes the process verifiable and trustworthy; preserve access to ballots and the counting elements so mistakes or fraud are discoverable and challengeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid electoral systems that force voters to accept the party leader's nominee
rubrics_metrics.description: Current practice compels electors either to vote for the nominee brought forward by local leaders or to abstain, producing candidates chosen by leaders rather than electors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral arrangements should prevent party bosses and local notabilities from imposing bland, unrepresentative candidates; allow competition from national figures and independent candidates so majorities are not enslaved to the least estimable portion of themselves.
